description:
No IP-based or user-based throttling on /api/query, /api/checkout, or /api/webhooks/*.

Impact: a single user can burn 30 free queries instantly, spam checkout sessions, or replay webhooks. Webhook replay protection is partly the responsibility of Stripe/Clerk signature verification, but no app-side defense exists.

Fix options:
- Redis sliding window (ioredis) — lowest latency, requires new dependency.
- Postgres token bucket: rate_limits(user_id, window_start, count) with upsert; reuse existing pg pool.
- Minimum acceptable: per-user 1s debounce on /api/query; per-user 5min cooldown on /api/checkout.

Files in scope:
- src/app/api/query/route.ts
- src/app/api/checkout/route.ts
- src/app/api/webhooks/clerk/route.ts
- src/app/api/webhooks/stripe/route.ts

Severity: MEDIUM — abuse/cost vector, not a direct breach.

resolution.test_function: denies and surfaces retryAfterSeconds when cooldown is active
resolution.note: Pg-backed token bucket. /api/query 1s, /api/checkout 5min. Webhooks deferred — Stripe/Clerk signature+replay protection covers them; revisit if abuse appears in logs. Requires migrations/005_rate_limits.sql to be applied in prod before deploy.
